title: `sidecar.istio.io/statsCompression` is removed and metrics-endpoint compression is on by default
quote: The annotation `sidecar.istio.io/statsCompression` was deprecated and removed. There now is the `statsCompression` option in proxyConfig to globally control compression support of the metrics endpoint
remediation: Drop the annotation from the listed pods; compression is now negotiated with the scraper's Accept-Encoding. To disable it per pod set `statsCompression: false` in the `proxy.istio.io/config` annotation, or globally in `meshConfig.defaultConfig`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations // {} | keys[] | startswith("sidecar.istio.io/statsCompression")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed pod carries the annotation 1.29 no longer reads

title: Ambient dry-run AuthorizationPolicies: enabling the new ztunnel support while old ztunnels remain makes them ENFORCE the dry-run policies

detection.reason: names the dry-run AuthorizationPolicies; whether the istiod flag is set is stated by the verify command

gate.reason: only an ambient (ztunnel) data plane is affected; a sidecar-only mesh has nothing to do

quote: Setting `AMBIENT_ENABLE_DRY_RUN_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY=true` will cause istiod to begin sending dry-run policies to ztunnel, using a new field in xDS. A ztunnel below version 1.29 will not support this field. As a result, older ztunnels will fully enforce these policies
remediation: Upgrade every ztunnel to 1.29 before setting `AMBIENT_ENABLE_DRY_RUN_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY=true` on istiod; until then leave the flag unset (istiod keeps withholding dry-run policies from ztunnel). The listed policies are the ones an old ztunnel would enforce.
verifyCommand: kubectl get authorizationpolicies.security.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["istio.io/dry-run"] == "true") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # each printed dry-run policy is enforced by a pre-1.29 ztunnel if AMBIENT_ENABLE_DRY_RUN_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY is turned on early

title: istiod debug endpoints now require authorization — Kiali and custom tooling in non-system namespaces are restricted

detection.reason: which tools call istiod's debug endpoints is not on the cluster; a Kiali Deployment is the known candidate

quote: Tools accessing debug endpoints from non-system namespaces (such as Kiali or custom monitoring tools) may be affected. Non-system namespaces are now restricted to config_dump, ndsz, and edsz endpoints for same-namespace proxies only.
remediation: Run Kiali (and any tool that reads istiod `/debug/*`) in the Istio root namespace, upgrade it to a release that copes with the restriction, or set `ENABLE_DEBUG_ENDPOINT_AUTH=false` on istiod to restore the old access.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("kiali/kiali"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + .spec.template.spec.containers[0].image'  # a printed Kiali outside the Istio root namespace loses most debug endpoints at 1.29 unless ENABLE_DEBUG_ENDPOINT_AUTH=false

title: Circuit-breaker `remaining_*` metrics are no longer tracked by default

detection.reason: which dashboards read the remaining_* series is not on the cluster; DestinationRules with connection-pool limits are the population whose metrics change

quote: Previously, these metrics were tracked by default. Now, tracking is disabled by default for better proxy memory usage.
remediation: Dashboards or alerts on `envoy_cluster_circuit_breakers_*_remaining_*` go empty after upgrade. Set `DISABLE_TRACK_REMAINING_CB_METRICS=false` on istiod (or use the compatibility version) to keep them; the DestinationRules with a `connectionPool` are where the limits being tracked are defined.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release|istio.io/release)/pilot"))) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(DISABLE_TRACK_REMAINING_CB_METRICS)$")) | $n + ": " + .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")'  # no printed line means remaining_* circuit-breaker metrics stop after upgrade

title: istio-cni now reconciles in-pod iptables rules of existing ambient pods on startup by default

detection.reason: a node-agent default; the istio-cni DaemonSet is the subject

quote: Iptables reconciliation is now enabled by default for ambient workloads in release 1.29.0. When a new `istio-cni` DaemonSet pod starts up, it will automatically inspect pods that were previously enrolled in the ambient mesh and upgrade their in-pod iptables/nftables rules
remediation: No action expected: after the istio-cni upgrade, already-enrolled ambient pods get their redirection rules brought up to date without a restart. Set `--set cni.ambient.reconcileIptablesOnStartup=false` to keep the old behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release|istio.io/release)/install-cni"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + ([.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("RECONCILE")) | .name + "=" + (.value // "")] | join(","))'  # no reconcile setting printed means the 1.29 default (on) applies

title: A TLSRoute's hostnames are narrowed to the listener's hostname

detection.reason: TLSRoute hostnames and the Gateway listeners they attach to are not compared; the TLSRoute CRD is the subject

quote: Previously, a TLSRoute with a broad hostname (e.g. `*.com`) attached to a listener with a narrower hostname (e.g. `*.example.com`) would incorrectly match the full route hostname instead of only the intersection (`*.example.com`), as required by the Gateway API spec.
remediation: SNI names a TLSRoute matched only because its hostname was broader than the listener's stop matching after the upgrade. Make each TLSRoute's hostnames fall within its listener's hostname, or widen the listener.
verifyCommand: kubectl get tlsroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " hostnames=" + ((.spec.hostnames // []) | join(",")) + " parents=" + ([.spec.parentRefs[]? | .name + "/" + (.sectionName // "*")] | join(","))'  # compare each hostname with its listener's hostname

title: A DestinationRule retryBudget without `percent` allows 20% retries instead of 0.2% (1.28.6, 1.29.2), and from 1.29.2 a top-level budget reaches subsets

detection.reason: the agent carries trafficPolicy key names, not retryBudget's fields or subsets' policies; DestinationRules with a top-level retryBudget are the population

quote: the default `percent` for `retryBudget` in `DestinationRule` was incorrectly set to 0.2% instead of the intended 20%.
remediation: Where a retryBudget sets no `percent`, Envoy now lets retries reach 20% of active requests instead of 0.2% (from 1.28.6 and 1.29.2), so a failing upstream sees up to 100x more retries. From 1.29.2 (not on the 1.28 line) a top-level retryBudget also applies to subsets with their own trafficPolicy, and a subset-level budget is honoured. Set `percent` explicitly to keep today's limit.
verifyCommand: kubectl get destinationrules.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.trafficPolicy.retryBudget != null or ([.spec.subsets[]?.trafficPolicy.retryBudget] | any)) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " percent=" + ((.spec.trafficPolicy.retryBudget.percent // "unset") | tostring)'  # unset means 20% after the upgrade

title: meshConfig.tlsDefaults.minProtocolVersion is enforced on downstream TLS as configured (it was mapped one or two versions too low)

detection.reason: meshConfig is not collected; istiod is the subject

quote: incorrect mapping of `meshConfig.tlsDefaults.minProtocolVersion` to `tls_minimum_protocol_version` in downstream TLS context.
remediation: Before the fix istiod cast the mesh enum straight to Envoy's, so TLSV1_2 was applied as TLS 1.0 and TLSV1_3 as TLS 1.1 on downstream SIMPLE/MUTUAL TLS (gateway servers and Sidecar ingress TLS without their own minProtocolVersion). After it, clients below the configured minimum are refused. If tlsDefaults.minProtocolVersion is set, confirm every client speaks at least that version.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -n istio-system -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.data.mesh != null) | "== " + .metadata.name, .data.mesh' | grep -E -A3 '^== |^tlsDefaults'  # a minProtocolVersion under tlsDefaults (not meshMTLS), other than TLS_AUTO, is enforced as written after the upgrade

title: A waypoint applies the routes of every VirtualService for a host, not only the first

detection.reason: which hosts have more than one VirtualService behind a waypoint is not compared; namespaces and Services using a waypoint are the population

quote: applying multiple VirtualService for the same hostname to waypoints.
remediation: Before the fix a waypoint used one VirtualService per host (as sidecars still do); after it, the routes of every VirtualService for that host are appended, gateway-style. A second, forgotten VirtualService for a waypoint-served host starts routing traffic. Before upgrading, make sure each such host has exactly the VirtualServices you mean.
verifyCommand: kubectl get virtualservices.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | .metadata.namespace as $n | .spec.hosts[]? | $n + " " + .] | group_by(.) | map(select(length != 1)) | .[] | .[0] + " x" + (length | tostring)'  # hosts with several VirtualServices; check the ones a waypoint serves

title: Wasm OCI pulls refuse a bearer-token realm on localhost, a metadata host or a private, loopback or link-local IP

detection.reason: WasmPlugin objects and their registries' token realms are not collected; istiod is the subject

remediation: A registry whose 401 challenge names a token realm on localhost, metadata.google.internal or a private/loopback/link-local IP literal (an in-cluster Harbor at https://10.x.x.x/service/token, for example) is refused, and the WasmPlugin stops loading; with failStrategy FAIL_CLOSE its traffic is denied. Serve the token endpoint under a DNS name before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get wasmplugins.extensions.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + .spec.url'  # curl -sI https://REGISTRY/v2/ and read the realm= in WWW-Authenticate

title: Gateway API CORS filters answer preflights from unlisted origins themselves and parse origins strictly

detection.reason: HTTPRoute CORS filters are not projected; the HTTPRoute CRD is the subject

quote: properly parse Gateway API Cors origin when wildcard is used, and ignore unmatched preflights.
remediation: A CORS preflight whose origin the route's filter does not allow is no longer forwarded to the backend (Envoy's unmatched-preflights policy becomes IGNORE), so a backend that answered CORS itself for other origins stops seeing them. Origins are parsed strictly. List every origin the route must allow in the filter before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get httproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.rules[]?.filters[]? | .type] | index("CORS")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # routes with a CORS filter

title: ztunnel resolves a hostname shared by a Service and ServiceEntries to the canonical one

detection.reason: which client namespaces define their own ServiceEntry for the host is not compared; ServiceEntries naming an in-cluster .svc host (the ones a Kubernetes Service now outranks) are the population. Ambient (ztunnel) only: a mesh without a ztunnel DaemonSet has no ztunnel to resolve through.

remediation: When a Kubernetes Service and ServiceEntries name the same host, ztunnel now resolves it for outbound traffic and DNS to the canonical one (the Service, else the oldest ServiceEntry) unless the client's own namespace defines one. A ServiceEntry that re-declared an in-cluster .svc host to change its ports, addresses or waypoint for clients in other namespaces stops applying to them: move it into each client namespace or drop it. Ambient (ztunnel) only: a mesh without a ztunnel DaemonSet can ignore this.
verifyCommand: kubectl get serviceentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.hosts[]? | test("[.]svc([.]|$)")] | any) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " hosts=" + (.spec.hosts | join(",")) + " created=" + .metadata.creationTimestamp'  # compare each with the Service of the same name: the Service wins outside this ServiceEntry's namespace

title: ztunnel attributes inbound traffic for a shared hostname to the canonical Service

detection.reason: which client namespaces define their own ServiceEntry for the host is not compared; ServiceEntries naming an in-cluster .svc host (the ones a Kubernetes Service now outranks) are the population. Ambient (ztunnel) only: a mesh without a ztunnel DaemonSet has no ztunnel to resolve through.

remediation: From 1.29.1 (1.30.0 on the next line) ztunnel matches inbound traffic for a hostname shared by a Service and ServiceEntries to the canonical one too, so the destination service in telemetry and the waypoint chosen for inbound traffic follow the Service rather than a ServiceEntry re-declaring its .svc host. Check dashboards and waypoint policies keyed on such a ServiceEntry. Ambient (ztunnel) only: a mesh without a ztunnel DaemonSet can ignore this.
verifyCommand: kubectl get serviceentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.hosts[]? | test("[.]svc([.]|$)")] | any) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " hosts=" + (.spec.hosts | join(",")) + " created=" + .metadata.creationTimestamp'  # compare each with the Service of the same name: the Service wins outside this ServiceEntry's namespace
